scope: User-facing surfaces of the DS-Hns Electron shell and of the official Harness UI as composed by the DS-Hns client plugin. READ-ONLY audit; only this file was written.

method.proven: The whole code path was read end to end in this checkout (registration -> render -> click handler -> route/IPC handler -> registry/allow-list).
method.suspected: Indirect evidence only (comment, doc, or a layer not read end to end); listed separately and never used to justify a PROVEN finding.
method.officialUiDefinition: The Harness web UI: the official shell (dsh-client-ui-layout, settings.section, conversation header) PLUS the surfaces the DS-Hns client plugin registers into its official slots (shell.overlay, settings.section). The Mega dock, the Mega tray, the Control Center and the separate always-on-top system-orb window are NOT the official UI.
method.notRun: No Electron app was launched and no HTTP request was executed; every claim is a static reading of this checkout.

auditState.why: The working tree was clean when this audit started (git status --porcelain was empty on the first command) and became dirty while it was being read: a concurrent agent in the same workspace was editing the very files under audit between 16:43 and 16:49 local time. This audit wrote only docs/acceptance/ui-surface-audit.json.
auditState.handling: Every finding was re-checked against the current working tree by grepping the exact code, and where the in-flight work has already closed a finding the entry is marked workingTreeStatus accordingly and its severity lowered to 'info' with the superseding evidence. Findings that survive carry workingTreeStatus 'still-present-reverified'. Line numbers are the ones read during the audit; when a citation moved, the re-verified line is given in workingTreeStatus.
inFlightWorkThatOverlapsThisAudit: A formal restart status/history is being added end to end: new app/plugins/restart-supervisor/status.cjs, pluginServices.restartStatus (app/plugin-host.cjs), controlCenter().restartStatus (app/extensions/mega/index.cjs), a '重启状态 / Restart status' section (app/extensions/mega/control-center.cjs) and view.restartStatus rendered on the Mega page (app/plugins/mega-core/lib/client.js, app/plugins/mega-core/lib/view.js).

The duplicate-ball problem is being closed: controlCenter().orb.mode ('system' when the always-on-top window is up) plus view.orb.hideInUi and an early 'return null' in MegaOrb (app/plugins/mega-core/lib/client.js).
Core task-continuity hooks are being threaded into the restart supervisor (app/core/task-continuity.cjs, app/plugins/mounted/index.cjs, app/plugin-host.cjs).

summary.headline: The plugin composes and all three official slots mount, but on the HEAD content the recovery-action row (id=null), the dashboard's only action (refresh-balance), 4 of 6 service actions, the whole advanced-policy surface, plugin permissions, the maintenance defer state and the human-gate count are dead or unrendered; the second ball (always-on-top window) is off by default. Two of these were being fixed in the dirty working tree while the audit ran (restart status/history, duplicate ball).

Nothing in the host enforces it, so a change to that one inline style would make the ball's wrapper swallow every click in the app.

negativeResults.detail: The in-UI store's loading state (client.js:328, 350-353, 969) is bounded: every host-half bridge call runs under a 4s AbortController (app/plugins/mega-core/lib/index.js:151-179) and every failure path sets loading:false or a reason. The new-task form's busy flag is cleared in a .finally (client.js:1726), and the loading prop on the official Button only reflects that flag. No code path was found that can leave a spinner or 'connecting' state pending indefinitely.
No display:none / opacity:0 / zero-size rule was found on either ball in its default state; see floatingBall.cssAndStacking.noDisplayOrOpacityBug.

Every panel id and element id declared by MEGA_FEATURES (app/extensions/mega/features.cjs:41-167) exists in app/extensions/mega/ui/dock.html (controlPanel, engineeringPanel, subWorkerPanel, queuePanel, balancePanel, computerUsePanel, hardwarePanel, skillsPanel, pluginsPanel, updatePanel, allowPeak, defaultAllowPeak, interruptRunningAtPeak) — no registry/markup desync there.

Every script referenced by dock.html exists, and every app/extensions/mega/ui/*.js is referenced except apply-skills-css.cjs (a .cjs helper) and orb.js (loaded by orb.html, itself unreachable by default) — no orphan dock module.

notes: Severity scale: high = a user-visible capability is offered but cannot work, or a required capability has no path at all; medium = reachable only outside the official UI, or a gate/registry that does not do what it declares; low = implemented-but-invisible detail; info = structural risk or documentation drift.

PROVEN vs SUSPECTED: all 25 findings are PROVEN by reading the full path; two of them additionally contain one explicitly SUSPECTED sub-claim each. They are (1) whether official dialogs actually cover the in-UI ball (the z-index of the primitives' Modal portal was not verified; see orb-zindex-bounded-by-overlay-layer) and (2) whether the tray can fail on a given host in practice (the failure path is proven, the failure is not; see dock-hidden-by-default-entry-points).

The working tree was being edited by a concurrent agent while this audit ran; 2 of the 25 findings were superseded by that in-flight work (restart history/status, duplicate ball) and 23 were re-verified as still present. See auditState.inFlightWorkThatOverlapsThisAudit and each finding's workingTreeStatus for the re-verification.

The single most consequential gap is the governance bridge's action allow-list (app/core/governance-bridge.cjs:36, 144): the official UI's entire action vocabulary (ServiceActions in view.js:292-311, MEGA_ACTIONS in view.js:30, refresh-balance) was designed against the shell's wider IPC handler (app/extensions/mega/index.cjs:1959-2055) and is only partially legal over the bridge the plugin actually talks to.

The shell-side action handler has its own gap in the opposite direction: SERVICE_ACTIONS is tested before the protection/store branches (app/extensions/mega/index.cjs:2036 vs 2039-2049), which captures 'check'/'enable'/'disable' for ids those branches were written for.

This checkout has no config/plugins/*.json and no data/plugins/installed.json, so the plugin world consists of the shipped set (app/plugins/mounted/index.cjs:607-635 plus accelerationPlugins()); the findings above were derived from that shipped configuration.
No Electron process was started and no HTTP request was issued during this audit; scripts/verify.ps1's source-text checks (e.g. line 271) cannot detect any of the runtime mismatches listed here.
